title: Synthetic change (made-up practice data)
summary: Twelve made-up monthly frames, each with its own normal, where a warm patch grows in the east, for practising the change from normal.
description: A pretend sea through one year: it is warmest in February and coolest in August, a little warmer in the north, with grey land on the west edge and a small island. From August to October a warm patch grows in the east, up to 1.5 °C above normal in October, then goes. Each month comes with its own normal, the same picture without the patch, so the change from normal is known exactly. The season is bigger than the patch, so the warmest date is not the date furthest above normal. Every temperature is chosen by us. None of it is real data.

regions.name: East patch
regions.description: A grid of 30 points in the east, inside the warm patch that grows from August to October.

regions.name: Open sea
regions.description: A grid of 30 points in open water west of the patch, which follows the seasons and nothing else.
